Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  1-day history of new-onset left-sided occipital throbbing headache, severity 8/10, minimal relief with single dose ibuprofen; no associated nausea, vomiting, visual disturbance, photophobia, neck stiffness, fever, rash, focal neurological symptoms. No prior headache history.  
- Relevant family medical history:  Mother – hypertension and migraines.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Ibuprofen (“Nurofen”) single dose yesterday; no regular medicines; no known drug allergies (NKDA).  
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Eats and drinks “normally”; specific diet and activity levels not discussed – not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Denies smoking, alcohol consumption, and recreational drug use.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Reports difficulty concentrating on work because of pain; no formal mood screening – not recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Denies blurred vision, visual aura, photophobia.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives with partner; occupation: designer.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth).

- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.  
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: First episode of severe unilateral occipital headache in 28-year-old woman, no red-flag symptoms or focal deficits identified on history. Family history significant for migraine. No current medications or comorbidities.

Working diagnosis: Probable primary headache disorder – migraine without aura most likely; tension-type or cervicogenic headache also considered.

Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):  
• Migraine without aura – high likelihood given unilateral throbbing pain, severity, family history, functional impairment.  
• Tension-type headache – moderate likelihood; lacks typical bilateral, band-like character.  
• Cervicogenic headache – lower likelihood; location compatible but no neck pain/positional component.

Plan: Trial stronger NSAID (name not specified) taken regularly with food, plus paracetamol as needed. Emphasized adequate hydration, rest. Safety-net advice: seek review if worsening pain, new neurological signs, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or recurrent episodes. Follow-up telehealth or in-person if no improvement within 1–2 days.

Management Plan

- Prescription: Stronger NSAID (dose/route/frequency not documented); may use paracetamol concurrently.  
- Advice: Rest, hydration, monitor symptoms.  
- Follow-up: Contact clinic if no improvement in 24–48 h or if red-flag symptoms develop.  
- Education: Discussed nature of headache and red-flag symptoms requiring urgent care.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: unilateral throbbing, severe, family history, age/sex typical.  
2. Tension-type headache – Moderate likelihood: persistent headache without neuro deficits but atypical unilateral nature.  
3. Cervicogenic headache – Low-moderate likelihood: unilateral occipital location; occupation may predispose though no neck symptoms.

Quality checks

● Missing expected elements: BP, pulse, temperature, full neurological exam, BMI, immunisation review, alcohol quantity screening, depression screening, cervical & STI screening status, medication name/dose, allergy confirmation, investigation plan.  
● No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx.
